purpose: Qualitative demand/friction intelligence for the boundary between employee sickness with employer sick pay, employment without sick pay, ordinary part-time work and partial sickness absence, inside the single Stödassistenten learning system. These scores are not measured search volumes and do not prove eligibility. Natural problem formulations are discovery signals; Försäkringskassan carries the truth-bearing current rules.

scoring.priority_rule: Prioritize combinations of high demand, high friction, high consequence and weak current product coverage; these scores are not measured search volumes.

natural_language_queries: jag jobbar deltid och är sjuk vem ska jag anmäla till
jag är timanställd och får ingen sjuklön vad gör jag
jag jobbar deltid och är sjukskriven resten
betyder deltid att jag får halv sjukpenning
vem betalar när jag är anställd och sjuk

demand_signal.basis: Employee sickness is a broad national situation and Försäkringskassan maintains separate current public guidance for employees with ordinary sick pay and employees without sick pay. The recurring part-time question adds a common boundary. This is a qualitative reach proxy, not measured search volume.

friction_signal.basis: Natural language often collapses employment extent, sickness-absence extent and payment route into one phrase. The route changes with whether the employer pays sick pay and whether part-time is ordinary work or partial sickness absence.

miss_consequence.basis: Choosing the wrong first reporting route or assuming a sickness-benefit percentage from ordinary part-time work can delay action or create false expectations about entitlement and payment.

source_fragmentation.basis: Försäkringskassan publishes neighbouring but distinct pages for employees with sick pay and employees without sick pay, while partial-sickness guidance sits inside the employee route. Users need the right branch before acting.

language_accessibility_friction.basis: Terms such as sjuklön, sjukpenning, normal working time and partial sickness absence are easy to conflate, especially when a user simply says that they work part-time and are sick.

steps_to_action.basis: The user first needs to establish whether employer sick pay applies, then distinguish ordinary part-time work from partial sickness absence, and then use the current employer/Försäkringskassan route without the product deciding eligibility.

recurrence_signal.basis: Försäkringskassan maintains dedicated guidance and FAQs for part-time sickness and a separate page for employees without sick pay, indicating a durable recurring information boundary.

current_product_coverage_gap.basis: The repository had a normalized employee-sickness support record and a generic person option for part-time sickness, but no focused public route that separates employer sick pay, no-sick-pay employment and ordinary part-time work from partial sickness absence.

signals.recommended_learning_action: Teach the existing shared product to recognize employee+sickness language, while explicitly deferring mixed jobseeker/employment cases to the existing v47 authority-disambiguation route. Ask whether employer sick pay applies before choosing the first route. Ask whether part-time means ordinary employment extent or reduced work due to sickness before giving partial-sickness worktime guidance. Do not infer eligibility, SGI, sickness percentage, diagnosis or amount.
signals.truth_rule: VERIFY reporting route and part-time sickness guidance against current Försäkringskassan primary sources. Do not infer no-sick-pay status merely from hourly employment, do not infer partial sickness absence from ordinary part-time work, and do not turn reporting guidance into an eligibility decision.
